unchanged_base.regression_test: original bounded scratch regression (32x512 inputs, before strengthening to 192x512 for chunk pressure) fails unchanged source: reserved bytes 134217728 -> 536870912; live bytes 901664 -> 428999200

mechanism.cause: m>16 dequantized a full f32 weight matrix for every queued GEMM; the 1024-dispatch batch retained many layers of dead matrices until submission.
mechanism.fix: Reuse one growable device scratch buffer across ordered dequantize/GEMM pairs. Keep its mutex through both dispatch recordings; retire grown buffers through existing deferred release. Retire scratch at existing explicit flush/readback. Use the existing recorder submission path with a 64-dispatch limit while batched GEMM scratch is active; explicit readback restores the normal 1024 limit. No allocator changes or pressure-triggered submissions remain.
mechanism.math: Same dequantization and GEMM shaders, dimensions, strides and accumulation order. Bind the allocated scratch capacity; the existing N/K push constants retain logical matrix bounds, including odd-width tiles. Packed original weights remain borrowed.
mechanism.transfers: No added host/device copies, repacking, second queue or runtime. The bounded prefill dispatch batch can add existing recorder submissions; no unconditional per-GEMM fence, allocation-time submission or GEMM-entry submission.
mechanism.lifetime: Raw scratch handles avoid an Arc cycle; shared-device concurrency and queued device destruction covered by regression tests.

reference.note: The unmodified batch-32 baseline crashes. The safe reference is exactly base 04d542d plus flush() after each m>16 dequantize/GEMM, preserving its shaders and arithmetic. --kernel production is the primary repair reference, using the same validated B50 CubeClNext selector as candidate. A second --kernel cubecl reference retains the previous three-format path with generic Q6_K. This is the existing kernel speed gate with a serialized prefill workaround, not a speedup claim against the crashing program.

protocol.inputs: Identical fixed teacher-forced inputs; full vocabulary compared at final prefill and every decode position. Timings include host logits and argmax. No concurrent builds, GPU tests or profiles during timed runs.

allocation_pressure_regression.note: Both allocation-time and GEMM-entry pressure submissions were rejected after full-model drift. Short checks were insufficient. Final code has no allocator changes and uses only the existing recorder post-dispatch submission boundary with a bounded prefill limit. The allocation lifetime test guards against early retirement of prepared arguments. No threshold was relaxed.

diagnostics_not_used_as_acceptance.initial_note: Initial scratch-only version retained an extra 128 MiB chunk during decode and failed memory gates. Comparison against the same production selector also failed speed gates (unchanged decode code); retained here, not counted as acceptance. A bounded prefill recorder limit fixed the chunk spill before final evaluation.
diagnostics_not_used_as_acceptance.cross_prefill_chunk_note: Safe batch32 vs historical chunk1 max full-logit difference 0.00024127960205078125. Different prefill GEMM reduction arithmetic predates this fix. No cross-chunk 1e-5 parity claim or relaxed threshold.

limitations: No concurrent-serving throughput acceptance or other GPU/backend evaluation.
The serial reference avoids OOM by synchronizing each GEMM; prefill speedup is relative to that workaround.
No cross-prefill-batch parity claim; same-batch arithmetic parity gate remains 1e-5.
